rule: S_N must not be null (mandatory one-to-one join key)
rationale: S_N is the primary join key with Acc_Info_dirty and must be populated for referential integrity. Evidence shows 0% missing but field is mandatory by design.

rule: S_N must be unique across the table
rationale: S_N acts as a primary identifier with one-to-one relationship to Acc_Info_dirty. Evidence confirms 30 distinct values for 30 records (100% unique).

rule: Every S_N in Cust_Bio_dirty must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N
rationale: Cross-table hint indicates one-to-one key relationship. Referential integrity must be enforced before joining.

rule: Account_No must not be null (mandatory account identifier)
rationale: Account_No is a mandatory business identifier. Evidence shows 0% missing values.

rule: Account_No should be unique (flag duplicates for business clarification)
rationale: Evidence shows 2 duplicate values (1001 and 1010) appearing twice each. While business may allow multiple customers per account, duplicates require verification.

rule: Account_No must be exactly 4 digits
rationale: Sample values show consistent 4-digit numeric format (1001-1028). Intended data type is string, suggesting identifier semantics.

rule: Name must not be null
rationale: Customer name is mandatory for identity. Evidence shows 0% missing values.

rule: Name must be in Title Case (except for lowercase particles: bin, binte, d/o, s/o)
rationale: Evidence shows case deviations: 'lim wei jie' (all lowercase) and 'WANG SHI JIE' (all uppercase). Standard naming convention requires Title Case.

check_params.logic: any(w[0].islower() or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o') and len(w) > 1)

rule: ID_No must not be null (mandatory government identifier)
rationale: Singapore NRIC/FIN is mandatory for customer identification. Evidence shows 0% missing values.

rule: ID_No must match Singapore NRIC/FIN format: one prefix letter (S/T/F/G), 7 digits, one checksum letter
rationale: 93.3% of values follow format S1234567D. Evidence flags deviations: 'F212233V' (6 digits) and '1916569C' (missing prefix).

rule: Race must be one of: Chinese, Malay, Indian
rationale: Evidence shows only three underlying categories with case variations (MALAY, malay, indian). Domain is restricted to these three values.

rule: Race must be in Title Case (Chinese, Malay, Indian)
rationale: Evidence shows inconsistent casing: 'MALAY', 'malay', 'indian'. Standardization to Title Case required.

rule: Gender must be either Male or Female
rationale: Evidence shows binary domain with case variations (male, FEMALE). Only two valid categories exist.

rule: Gender must be in Title Case (Male, Female)
rationale: Evidence shows inconsistent casing: 'male', 'FEMALE'. Standardization to Title Case required.

rule: Age must be numeric and parseable as an integer
rationale: Column contains text value 'Twenty-five' which cannot be parsed as numeric. Evidence flags 1 non-numeric value (3.3%).

rule: Age must be between 13 and 120 (realistic service account age range)
rationale: Evidence flags values below 13 (-5 and 4) as unrealistic for a service account. Domain constraint applies regardless of observed sample min/max.

rule: Contact_No must not be null (mandatory contact field)
rationale: Evidence shows 6.7% missing values (2 records). Contact number is typically mandatory for customer records.

rule: Contact_No must be a valid Singapore phone number (8 digits, optional +65 or 65 prefix)
rationale: Sample shows Singapore country code (65) and 8-digit local numbers. One value '8964359' has only 7 digits. Valid range is 7-15 digits per E.164, but Singapore local numbers are exactly 8 digits.

rule: Email must not be null
rationale: Email is mandatory for customer communication. Evidence shows 0% missing values.

rule: Email must contain exactly one @ symbol with no whitespace
rationale: Evidence flags 4 structurally malformed emails: 'not-an-email' (missing @), 'useremail.com' (missing @), 'zx91 @example.com' (contains space), 'nabilah@@example.com' (double @).

rule: Country must not be null
rationale: Country is mandatory for address validation. Evidence shows 0% missing values.

rule: Country must be standardized to 'Singapore' (flag variants: SG, S'pore, Singapura, 新加坡, etc.)
rationale: Evidence shows 8 distinct representations of Singapore. Business requires standardization to single canonical form 'Singapore'.

rule: Street_Name must not be null
rationale: Street name is mandatory for address completeness. Evidence shows 0% missing values.

rule: Street_Name must be in Title Case (not all uppercase)
rationale: Evidence shows 'HOLLAND ROAD' in all-caps format while 29 other values use Title Case. Standardization required.

rule: Postal_Code must not be null
rationale: Postal code is mandatory for address validation. Evidence shows 0% missing values.

rule: Postal_Code must be a 6-digit code
rationale: Dominant observed format is 6 digits (derived from the data distribution). Values of different lengths are likely truncated, padded, or sentinel values.

rule: Name particles must be consistent with Gender (Bin/s/o indicates Male; Binte/d/o indicates Female)
rationale: Malay and Indian naming conventions use gender-specific particles. 'Bin' and 's/o' indicate male; 'Binte' and 'd/o' indicate female. Mismatches indicate data quality issues.

check_params.logic: (bool(re.search(r'(?<![a-z0-9])(?:bin|bin|s/o|s/o|s/o|s/o)(?![a-z0-9])', str(str(row['Name'])).lower())) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'male') or (bool(re.search(r'(?<![a-z0-9])(?:binte|binte|d/o|d/o|d/o|d/o)(?![a-z0-9])', str(str(row['Name'])).lower())) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'female')

rule: If Country is Singapore (in any form), Postal_Code must be exactly 6 digits
rationale: Singapore postal codes are strictly 6 digits. Validates that short postal codes (6907, 99999) are flagged when country is Singapore.

check_params.logic: str(row['Country']).strip().lower() in ['singapore', 'sg', 's\'pore', 'republic of singapore', 'singapura', '新加坡'] and (pd.isna(row['Postal_Code']) or len(str(int(row['Postal_Code']))) != 6)

rule: ID_No must match the corresponding ID value in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: S_N is a one-to-one join key. The government ID should be consistent across both tables for the same individual. Sample shows potential mismatch (S8421753J vs S8421753X).

check_params.semantic_check: ID_No must exactly match ID for the same S_N

rule: Name must match the corresponding Full_Name in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N (accounting for case standardization)
rationale: S_N is a one-to-one join key. Customer name should be consistent across both tables. Sample shows case differences (WANG SHI JIE vs Wang Shi Jie) that should be flagged for standardization.

check_params.semantic_check: Name must match Full_Name for the same S_N after case normalization
